results.content:
Trump remains weakest among younger voters. Among those aged 18 to 34, just 22 percent approve of his job performance, compared with 72 percent who disapprove, according to the newest Civiqs data.

Among voters aged 35 to 49, approval stands at 29 percent, while 63 percent disapprove.

Independents also remain negative, with 28 percent approving and 64 percent disapproving. Women disapprove by a 65-to-30 margin, while men are divided at 53 percent disapprove to 42 percent approve. According to Civiqs, last updated August 12, Trump's net approval in New Jersey stood at -35%.

New Jersey tilts unfavorable overall. About 65% of New Jersey residents polled currently disapprove of the president's performance.About 30% approve and another 5% did not choose either.

Education: Respondents across all education levels disapprove of Trump’s job performance, with postgraduate at 78%, college graduate at 67% and non-college graduate at 60%. Meanwhile, Republicans were the most favorable toward Trump, with 82% approving of Trump's job performance.

results.content:
The data comes from Civiqs’ rolling online tracking poll of 118,886 registered voters. A Newsweek analysis compares Trump’s approval rating on July 22, 2026, with where it stood on January 20, 2025, the first day of his second term, with net approval calculated as 'approve' minus 'disapprove.'

Nationally, Trump receives 38 percent approval and 57 percent disapproval, leaving him 19 points underwater overall.

results.content:
When asked in April 2025, Trump's first three months were rated at 61% approval by Oklahoman polltakers. Now in August 2026, Trump remains at 52% approval in Oklahoma.

Nationally, Trump has an unfavorable majority across all ages, education levels, genders, and races. Trump's only favorability among Civiqs' demographics is found in the 82% of Republicans who remain faithful to the president. [...] According to Civiqs, the Republican president holds a strong approval rating in Oklahoma among several demographics, including all poll takers 35 and older, postgraduate-educated individuals, non-Republicans and non-white people.

Oklahoma's party lines mimic that of the national level. Oklahoma D
